note: Known high/critical advisories in production dependencies, each named with the ticket
that owns the fix. The gate (scripts/check-audit.mjs) fails on any high/critical
advisory NOT listed here, so this file is the line between 'debt we have already
booked' and 'something new'.
Adding an entry is an explicit, reviewable decision — give the id, the package, and
the ticket or reason. Removing entries is the point: the weekly audit workflow fails
when a listed advisory is no longer reported, so a fix prunes its own line.
The single entry below is booked against #246, which upgrades tailwindcss 3 → 4 and so
takes `braces` out of the production graph entirely. That same PR deletes this entry
again, because the weekly `--strict` run fails on a booked advisory that no longer
reports. The entry exists so the commits before the upgrade are not red.
Before it the list was EMPTY, and that was a real state rather than a missing file. It
was 27 entries — booked on 2026-08-06/07 against #101 and #104 — and #101 cleared all
of them: an in-range `pnpm update` (the lockfile was sitting at the floor of ranges
that already allowed the patched versions), one devDependency pin raised so tailwindcss
would stop deduping onto a vulnerable postcss, and #104's swiper 12 major before it.
Two entries needed no fix of their own. The `image-size` pair had no published patch
and were expected to sit here for a while; payload 3.87.1 dropped the dependency, so
they left the graph instead of being waited out. Worth remembering the next time an
unpatched transitive looks permanent.
An empty list also retires the gate's old 'the audit stopped looking' tell (zero
findings against a non-empty baseline). check-audit.mjs now checks the size of the
graph it walked instead — see the comment there before assuming a green run means
anything.

advisories.GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm: braces — stack-exhaustion DoS through deeply nested patterns, no published fix. Reaches the production graph only through tailwindcss 3. #246 upgrades to tailwindcss 4 (zero dependencies) and deletes this line.
